faq.question: Do I need to come to the office in person to start a case?
faq.answer: No. The first conversation can happen through the contact form or by phone. Showing up in person at the office is usually only needed at the stage of filing the application — we let you know beforehand whenever it's necessary.

faq.question: How long does a residence card procedure take?
faq.answer: It depends on the office and the type of case — anywhere from a few months to over a year during busy periods. During the initial conversation we tell you what timeframe to realistically expect for your specific procedure.

faq.question: What happens if my legal stay expires while the case is pending?
faq.answer: Filing a complete application before your legal stay ends usually entitles you to remain in Poland for the duration of the proceedings — confirmed by the relevant stamp in your passport. We check this individually for every case.

faq.question: Do you handle cases outside Warsaw?
faq.answer: We fully handle cases where the competent authority is the Mazovian Voivodeship Office or a Warsaw district office. In other regions we can advise, but we do not represent clients before the local office.

faq.question: How much does it cost to have you handle a case?
faq.answer: The cost depends on the type of procedure and how complex it is. We give a quote after the initial conversation, once we know the scope of work — not before.

karta-pobytu-czasowego.title: Temporary residence card
karta-pobytu-czasowego.summary: Temporary residence permit — work, study, staying with family, or another basis.
karta-pobytu-czasowego.intro: A temporary residence permit is the most common way to legalize a stay in Poland. The application is filed in person at the voivodeship office responsible for the place of stay, no later than the last day of legal stay.
who: People working in Poland under a contract
Students and doctoral candidates
Family members of someone living in Poland
People running a business
documents: A completed application and four photographs
A valid travel document (passport) with a copy of every page
Documents confirming the purpose of stay (contract, university certificate, marriage certificate)
Proof of health insurance
Documents confirming a stable source of income
Proof of address
help: We work out the correct legal basis for the application and check whether the deadline still holds
We assemble and verify the documents before filing
We draft the justification for the application
We respond to office requests to complete missing information
We represent you in the proceedings under a power of attorney

pobyt-staly.title: Permanent residence and long-term EU resident status
pobyt-staly.summary: An indefinite permit for holders of the Pole's Card, spouses of Polish citizens, and after years of legal stay.
pobyt-staly.intro: A permanent residence permit is issued for an indefinite period, though the residence card itself must be renewed every ten years. Long-term EU resident status is a separate procedure, available after an uninterrupted stay in Poland.
who: Holders of the Pole's Card
Spouses of Polish citizens, after the required period of marriage and residence
Children of Polish citizens or of people with a permanent residence permit
People after the required period of uninterrupted legal stay
documents: A completed application and four photographs
A valid travel document with a copy
Documents confirming the basis for applying for the permit
Documents confirming an uninterrupted stay in Poland
For EU resident status: proof of Polish language knowledge, stable income and insurance
help: We check whether the period of stay counts as uninterrupted
We choose whichever procedure is more advantageous for your situation
We assemble documentation confirming your residence history
We handle correspondence with the office

zezwolenie-na-prace.title: Work permit
zezwolenie-na-prace.summary: Type A and C permits, declarations of entrusting work, seasonal work — for both employee and employer.
zezwolenie-na-prace.intro: It is the employer, not the foreign national, who applies for a work permit. We help both sides: the employee to check that their work is legal, and the employer to run the procedure without formal errors.
who: Employers hiring foreign nationals
Employees changing employer or position
Temporary employment agencies
People doing seasonal work
documents: The employer's application together with the company's registration documents
The foreign national's travel document
Documents confirming qualifications, if required for the position
The starost's opinion, if required
Proof of fee payment
help: We work out which type of permit applies to the position
We check whether a labour market test is required
We prepare the documentation on the employer's side
We advise on changes to employment terms while the permit is valid

zaproszenie-dla-rodziny.title: Invitation for family
zaproszenie-dla-rodziny.summary: Registering an invitation in the register of invitations — a document family members need for a visa application.
zaproszenie-dla-rodziny.intro: An invitation registered by the voivode confirms that the host will provide accommodation and cover the costs of stay for the invited person. It is one of the documents submitted with a visa application.
who: People inviting family members for a visit
Foreign nationals with a valid residence permit in Poland
Polish citizens inviting relatives from abroad
documents: An application to register the invitation

Documents confirming the ability to cover the costs of stay

help: We complete the application and check the required financial thresholds

wymiana-prawa-jazdy.title: Driving licence exchange
wymiana-prawa-jazdy.summary: Exchanging a foreign driving licence for a Polish one, without retaking a course where possible.
wymiana-prawa-jazdy.intro: A foreign driving licence can be exchanged for a Polish one if it was issued by a country that is party to the relevant convention. In some cases a theory exam is required; in others the exchange happens without one.

People whose period of recognition for a foreign document is ending
Professional drivers who need a Polish document
documents: An application for the licence exchange
The original foreign driving licence together with a sworn translation
A photograph meeting the requirements
A document confirming residence in Poland
help: We check whether the document is eligible for exchange and whether an exam is required
We arrange the sworn translation
We file the application at the communications department

pesel-i-meldunek.title: PESEL number and address registration
pesel-i-meldunek.summary: Assigning a PESEL number and registering an address — the basis for tax matters, healthcare and e-government services.
pesel-i-meldunek.intro: A PESEL number and address registration open access to most official matters: tax settlements, registering with a doctor, setting up a Trusted Profile. Both are handled at the district office.
who: People who have just moved to Poland
People changing their place of residence
Parents registering a child born in Poland
documents: An identity document
A document confirming legal title to the property or the owner's consent
An application for a PESEL number stating the legal basis
A form reporting permanent or temporary residence
help: We work out the correct legal basis for assigning the PESEL number
We prepare the forms and check the property documents
We arrange an appointment at the district office

profil-zaufany.title: Trusted Profile
profil-zaufany.summary: Setting up and confirming a Trusted Profile — an electronic signature for official matters.
profil-zaufany.intro: A Trusted Profile lets you handle official matters online and sign applications electronically. Setting it up requires a PESEL number and identity confirmation at a confirmation point or through Polish online banking.
who: People who already have a PESEL number
People filing applications through mObywatel or ePUAP
Business owners handling company matters online
documents: PESEL number
An identity document
Access to Polish online banking, or a visit to a confirmation point
help: We walk you through the registration step by step
We point out the fastest available method of identity confirmation
We help with your first applications filed electronically

about.title: About the firm
paragraphs: Residence cases are rarely just a formality. Behind every application is a job, a home, a child's school, or a deadline that starts running at the worst possible moment. That's why the first conversation is about the situation, not the form.

We handle cases before the Mazovian Voivodeship Office and Warsaw's district offices. We deal with legalizing residence and work, as well as the related matters that make everyday life in Poland harder without them: a PESEL number, address registration, driving licence exchange, or a Trusted Profile.
Clients talk to us in the languages they actually know. We handle cases in Polish, English, Ukrainian and Russian.
